html:
The realm of Lysimachus, one of Alexander the Great's generals, centred on Thrace. The map shows it in 300 BCE, on both sides of the straits between Europe and Asia.

When Alexander died in 323 BCE, Lysimachus was given Thrace to govern. He spent years fighting the Thracian tribes, among them the Odrysian king Seuthes, and founded a new capital, Lysimachia, on the Gallipoli peninsula. Like the other generals in the Wars of the Diadochi, he took the title of king in 306 or 305 BCE.

In 301 BCE he joined Seleucus to defeat Antigonus at the Battle of Ipsus and gained most of western Asia Minor. Later he took Macedon as well, and for a few years ruled the largest kingdom in the Aegean. Family murders weakened him, and in 281 BCE the old king was killed fighting Seleucus at Corupedium. His kingdom fell apart, and soon after, Celtic raiders swept into Thrace. To the west lay the Kingdom of Kassander.
